title: Faten Hamama's birth chart
metaDescription: Faten Hamama's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 5.2° Gemini. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Cardinal signs carry five of the ten placements whose signs are settled — the broadest certain weighting in the chart. Cardinal weight is read as initiative: the instinct to be the reason something began.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 5.2° Gemini, inside the first decan (0°–10°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Mercury. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Taurus (10.4°), Venus in Taurus (7.6°), Mars in Leo (22.7°): thought with its feet on the ground, attraction that grows by reliability, effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Jupiter to Pluto, a conjunction with 0.1° of slack. A conjunction is the least negotiable aspect in the scheme — no distance to argue across, so the pair arrives as a single instinct. Behind it, Uranus square Pluto at 1.3°, and Jupiter square Uranus at 1.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Saturn while both square Uranus. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags three placements in this chart. Venus in Taurus at 7.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Cancer at 19.3° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Capricorn at 22.8° is in domicile. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 earth, 2 air, 2 fire, 2 water by element and 5 cardinal, 3 fixed, 2 mutable by modality. Earth signs hold the scheme’s slow end, where results are measured in what survives rather than what starts. Saturn was retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Libra for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.3° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 9.6°.
